title: HEARTLAND Protocol App — Clinical Implementation Companion for Rural Heart Failure
description: HEARTLAND Protocol App is an educational clinical implementation companion for rural and resource-limited heart failure settings. Version 1.11.0 records medication schedules against the patient’s local day, stores all ten explicit inputs and the scoring version with a risk assessment, and reconciles scoped alerts when staff reconnect. An explicit patient action records a portal message as read. Reports and exports carry corrected laboratory observations, medication doses and date boundaries appropriate to their format. Visitors can follow a fictional case from the sandbox queue to the recorded human decision and return through a shareable link. The visual interface uses the HEARTLAND website’s typography and color palette, with labeled statuses, keyboard navigation, enlarged chart readings and high-contrast forms. The existing bilingual check-ins, simulated outreach, language assistance and 58 released synthetic recordings remain available. The article, implementation toolkit and companion software have separate publication records.
notes: The public demonstration uses fictional cases. Authenticated workflows support controlled evaluation. Verification covers software behavior, access boundaries, exports and browser accessibility checks. A portal read receipt records the explicit action of the signed-in user. Clinical validation, prospective patient outcomes and institutional readiness require separate evidence. The HEARTLAND Risk Stratification Framework remains proposed pending validation. This software release does not authorize real patient data or unsupervised clinical use.
